To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pour point of waxy hydrocarbon solvents is determined by the volume fraction of precipitated crystals and that the pour point depressant polymers work, by increasing the axial ratios of the crystals.

(a) the pour point temperature is a function of the wax crystal axial (plate) ratio (h/d) and that (b) the pour point depressants (PPDs) work by increasing (h/d) of the wax crystal platelets, thereby increasing the volume fraction of wax crystals at the pour point and reducing the pour-point temperature.
(1) Pour point depression is achieved by increasing the volume fraction of the wax crystals at the pour point transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding of the mechanism of pour point depression.
how the addition of polymer additives affects the pour point of a mixture containing wax crystals.
the effect of polymer additives on the pour point transition of hydrocarbon solvent systems containing wax crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPD polymers reduce the pour point temperature of wax-solvent mixtures by increasing the wax axial ratio and, thereby, the volume fraction of wax crystals at the pour point.
the pour point temperature is determined by a combination of wax crystal axial ratio, the wax solubility boundary, and the ability of the PPD to modify the wax solubilisation process.
the pour point of wax-solvent mixtures can be predicted by ideal solution thermodynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pour point temperature is controlled by the precipitation of wax crystals with axial ratios (0.005- 0.05) at a volume fraction of crystals larger than 2.5 to 11 times the axial ratio.
the pour point depression is a function of wax crystal shape and the ability of the PPD to alter the wax crystal shape.

the pour point of wax-solvent systems is determined by the volume fraction of precipitated wax crystals and that the pour point can be reduced by increasing the volume fraction at which precipitation occurs, which is accomplished by modifying the wax crystal shape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given PPD, its efficacy depends on its ability to increase the axial ratio of the crystals, which, in turn, depends on the wax-solvent system and the PPD-solvent system.

, to reduce the pour point temperature of a wax-solvent system, the PPD should be a polymer with the following properties: 1. it is soluble in both the solvent and the wax; 2. it adsorbs onto the crystal-solution interface; 3. it is capable of modifying the crystal shape, and 4. the solubility of the polymer in the solvent is close to the solubility boundary temperature of the wax.

, in wax-containing hydrocarbon solvents, pour point depression is caused by a reduction in the volume fraction of precipitated wax crystals, and that this reduction is achieved by increasing the axial ratio of the precipitated wax crystals.
